rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow, administrability-focused opinion upholding § 2(c) as a viewpoint-neutral, objective consent condition on access to the federal registration bundle, distinguishing Tam and Brunetti as involving discretionary message-policing. Separate writings are most likely from the dissenters emphasizing the “veto” over political criticism and from one or more conservatives (especially Thomas/Gorsuch/Alito) to frame the First Amendment analysis in benefit/contours-of-program and historical/publicity-interest terms.
